briefing.exam_subtitle: Next-Generation NCLEX (NGN) Exam Readiness Assessment • Case 01 • Medical-Surgical
briefing.candidate_instructions: You are the receiving RN on the Medical-Surgical floor. John Doe (62M) has just arrived from PACU (4 hours post-exploratory laparotomy). You have 5:00 minutes to complete your admission safety checks, recognize any acute physiological cues, intervene appropriately, and escalate care.
exam_rules: The 5:00 clock starts when you enter the room and cannot be paused.
The simulation never acts on your behalf. Every assessment and intervention must be initiated by you.
Station labels are neutral. Findings are only revealed after you walk to and inspect a station.
No feedback is given during the bedside phase. All decisions are scored after you exit.
The bedside phase ends when you select [Conclude Bedside Care & Escalate (SBAR)], when time expires, or if the patient remains in critical hypoxia.
briefing.controls_hint: Move: WASD / Arrow keys or click the floor • Inspect: click a station (the nurse walks there first) • Close a station panel: Esc
briefing.controls_hint_touch: Move: Tap the floor or use the bottom Walk bar • Inspect: Tap a station pin or Walk bar button • Camera: 1-finger drag to orbit, 2-finger pinch to zoom

conclude_confirm.title: Conclude bedside care?
conclude_confirm.body: You will leave the room and cannot return. You will then complete the SBAR escalation and follow-up questions.

end_reasons.STUDENT_CONCLUDED: You concluded bedside care and escalated to the surgical resident.
end_reasons.CODE_BLUE_FAILURE: The patient remained in critical hypoxia (SpO2 below 80%) for more than 30 seconds. A Code Blue was called and the bedside phase ended.

POWER_ON_MONITOR.label: Powered on bedside monitor (SpO2 probe + ECG leads)
POWER_ON_MONITOR.rationale: Continuous SpO2 and ECG telemetry establishes the baseline needed to recognize post-operative deterioration.

VERIFY_PATIENT_ID.label: Verified wristband with two identifiers
VERIFY_PATIENT_ID.rationale: Two-identifier verification (name + DOB) is required before any intervention or medication.

FLAG_ALLERGY.label: Flagged penicillin anaphylaxis allergy
FLAG_ALLERGY.rationale: Cefazolin is a cephalosporin; a history of penicillin anaphylaxis requires prescriber clarification before administration.

CEFAZOLIN_HELD_ALLERGY.label: Cefazolin held — prescriber clarification required
CEFAZOLIN_HELD_ALLERGY.rationale: Holding the cephalosporin pending clarification prevents a potential cross-sensitivity anaphylactic reaction.

ALLERGY_CROSS_SENSITIVITY_ERROR.label: Administered Cefazolin 1 g IV without flagging penicillin anaphylaxis
ALLERGY_CROSS_SENSITIVITY_ERROR.rationale: Patients with penicillin anaphylaxis can cross-react with cephalosporins. The allergy must be flagged and the order clarified before administration.

SET_BED_FOWLERS.label: Elevated head of bed (Fowler's)
SET_BED_FOWLERS.rationale: Elevating the head of bed lowers the diaphragm and improves lung expansion and oxygenation.

SET_BED_FLAT.label: Set bed flat supine (0°)
SET_BED_FLAT.rationale: Flat supine does not support ventilation in a hypoxic post-abdominal-surgery patient.

TRENDELENBURG_TRAP.label: Placed patient in Trendelenburg (-15°)
TRENDELENBURG_TRAP.rationale: Head-down positioning pushes abdominal organs against the diaphragm, reducing lung expansion and worsening hypoxia.

ADMINISTER_O2.label: Initiated supplemental oxygen
ADMINISTER_O2.rationale: Supplemental O2 per the PRN order treats hypoxemia — but can mask ongoing opioid hypoventilation if the opioid source is not addressed.

PAUSE_PCA.label: Paused morphine PCA infusion
PAUSE_PCA.rationale: Stopping the opioid source is the priority intervention for opioid-induced respiratory depression.

OPIOID_DEMAND_BOLUS_TRAP.label: Administered 1 mg morphine PCA demand bolus
OPIOID_DEMAND_BOLUS_TRAP.rationale: An additional opioid dose in a drowsy, hypoxic patient with shallow respirations worsens opioid toxicity (RR fell to 6/min, SpO2 79%). Pain must not be treated with more opioid while respiratory depression is present.

CONTINUE_BASAL_TRAP.label: Continued basal morphine infusion (2 mg/hr)
CONTINUE_BASAL_TRAP.rationale: Continuing the basal rate leaves the source of respiratory depression running.

SALINE_FLUSH_TRAP.label: Rapid normal-saline flush of the PCA line
SALINE_FLUSH_TRAP.rationale: A rapid flush pushes the residual morphine in the tubing into the patient as an unintended bolus.

PREPARE_NALOXONE.label: Prepared naloxone 0.4 mg IV (PRN order)
PREPARE_NALOXONE.rationale: Having the opioid antagonist ready supports rapid reversal if respiratory depression progresses.

ADMINISTER_NALOXONE.label: Administered naloxone 0.4 mg IV push
ADMINISTER_NALOXONE.rationale: Naloxone reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression. Monitor closely: it is shorter-acting than morphine.

NALOXONE_NOT_INDICATED.label: Administered naloxone outside PRN parameters
NALOXONE_NOT_INDICATED.rationale: The PRN order specifies RR < 10 or SpO2 < 90%. Unnecessary reversal can precipitate severe pain and withdrawal.

BLIND_INTERVENTION_PENALTY.label: Intervention performed before admission safety checks
BLIND_INTERVENTION_PENALTY.rationale: Power on the monitor, verify the wristband ID, and review the MAR and allergies before intervening.

OPIOID_MASKING_BRADYPNEA.label: Patient became bradypneic (opioid infusion continued)
OPIOID_MASKING_BRADYPNEA.rationale: With morphine still infusing, supplemental O2 masked hypoventilation until RR fell to 8/min.

UNTREATED_HYPOXIA_DETERIORATION.label: Untreated hypoxia deteriorated (SpO2 84%)
UNTREATED_HYPOXIA_DETERIORATION.rationale: 60 seconds without oxygen or head-of-bed elevation.

RENARCOTIZATION.label: Re-sedation after naloxone (PCA still infusing)
RENARCOTIZATION.rationale: Naloxone wears off before morphine; the infusion must be stopped.

exit_questions.title: Question 1 of 2 • SBAR Escalation
exit_questions.prompt: You call the surgical resident about John Doe. Which SBAR report is most appropriate?

options.text: S: John Doe, 62, is in pain after his surgery and can't get comfortable. B: He had an exploratory laparotomy today. A: He seems uncomfortable and his oxygen is a little low. R: Can you increase the morphine PCA basal rate so he can rest?

S: John Doe, 62, 4 h post-exploratory laparotomy, with suspected opioid-induced respiratory depression. B: Morphine PCA 2 mg/hr basal + 1 mg demand; severe penicillin allergy (anaphylaxis); cefazolin due. A: Arrived drowsy with SpO2 88%, shallow RR; PCA paused, HOB elevated, O2 applied; ABG pending. R: Please evaluate at the bedside now, review the analgesia plan, confirm naloxone parameters, and clarify the cefazolin order.

S: I'm calling with an update on John Doe. B: He came up from PACU this afternoon. A: His SpO2 is 88% and his RR is 26. R: No orders needed right now — I'll keep monitoring him and call back if anything changes.
S: John Doe's cefazolin is due. B: He is on a morphine PCA. A: I gave the cefazolin and he is resting with his eyes closed. R: Please renew the PCA order for tonight.

exit_questions.rationale: Option B follows SBAR structure, states the suspected problem, includes the relevant background (opioid PCA, penicillin anaphylaxis), reports the assessment and interventions already taken, and makes a specific, safe recommendation. A requests more opioid, C makes no recommendation despite abnormal findings, and D reports a medication error as routine.

exit_questions.title: Question 2 of 2 • ABG & Pharmacology Follow-Up
exit_questions.prompt: Fifteen minutes later an arterial blood gas is drawn: pH 7.28, PaCO2 55 mmHg, PaO2 62 mmHg, HCO3 24 mEq/L. The patient is difficult to arouse with RR 9/min. Which interpretation and nursing action are most appropriate?

options.text: Metabolic acidosis — prepare sodium bicarbonate IV push.
Uncompensated respiratory acidosis — increase the morphine PCA basal rate, because pain-related splinting is causing hypoventilation.
Uncompensated respiratory acidosis — administer naloxone 0.4 mg IV per the PRN order, keep the PCA paused, and remain with the patient to monitor for re-sedation.
Compensated respiratory alkalosis — coach the patient to slow his breathing.

exit_questions.rationale: pH < 7.35 with PaCO2 > 45 mmHg and a normal HCO3 is uncompensated respiratory acidosis. With RR 9/min on a morphine PCA, this is opioid-induced hypoventilation: naloxone per the PRN order reverses it, the opioid source stays off, and the nurse monitors for re-sedation because naloxone is shorter-acting than morphine.

ehr_tabs.notes: 14:00 — Patient transferred from PACU 4 hours ago following abdominal exploratory surgery. Drowsy, easily distracted. Receiving continuous IV Morphine PCA (2 mg/hr basal rate + 1 mg demand bolus every 15 min). Respirations shallow and rapid.
ehr_tabs.mar:
1. Morphine Sulfate 2 mg/hr IV PCA continuous + 1 mg bolus Q15m PRN (ACTIVE)
2. Supplemental Oxygen via Nasal Cannula (2-6 L/min) or Mask PRN for SpO2 < 92%
3. Naloxone (Narcan) 0.4 mg IV push PRN for opioid-induced respiratory depression / RR < 10 or SpO2 < 90%
4. Cefazolin 1 g IV Q8H — scheduled dose DUE NOW
